title: Source Files and Delivery Files
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Three zones sort common file formats into good source, usually acceptable, and poor source, with two badges that separate "is the format open?" from "is it a good source for editing?".

educational.topic: Open file formats versus good editable source formats
learningObjectives: The learner will explain why an open file format is not always a good source for editing, using the PDF as the example.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Could someone edit this file and keep its structure?
commonMisconceptions: An open format is an editable format
A PDF is a good way to share something others will change
assessmentOpportunities: Is a PDF an open format? Is it a good source?
Why is a Word document only usually acceptable?
Which formats are good sources for data and for diagrams?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
